label: GO step after a rewarded trial, when the agent is confidently choosing a1
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward == 1, 100% of mass), and almost only when the agent is about to choose a1 (99.99% of mass) with a very strong a1 policy logit (all activations are in the top choice-logit bin, > 8.07). Since prev_reward==1 and a1 choice essentially imply a stay after a rewarded a1->S1 trial, it reads as a confident win-stay-on-a1 unit (essentially never after a rare or a2 trial). An observed-only version without the model logit, GO & prev_reward==1 & action==1 & prev_state!=2, gets recall ~1.0 but precision 0.53 (dev F1 0.70); the choice > 8 condition is the agent own computed policy, not a future outcome, so I recorded it. Magnitude: strongest right after a reward that follows an unrewarded/rare trial, and it decays steadily over long runs of consecutive rewarded a1 trials (e.g. 0.81, 0.71, 0.59, 0.47, 0.35 across a streak) before dropping out, so it acts like a novelty/surprise signal more than a plain streak counter. It also fades late in the episode (no activations at ep_trial 90-99); adding ep_trial < 85 raises dev F1 from 0.81 to 0.86. It does not fire after unrewarded trials, before a2 choices, or at D1/D2.

issues: Core factual claims hold. The unit fires only at GO (D1/D2 have 0 activations). prev_reward==1 carries 100% of mass, and prev_reward==0 with choice>8 gives 29339 steps and 0 activations, so the reward gating is real and not just a side effect of the logit. Every activation falls in the choice > 8.07 bin. The upcoming action is a1 on 58461 of 58467 activations. Only 3 activations come after a prev a2 trial and 3 after a prev rare transition.

Systematic false-positive class that the recorded predicate leaves in: late episode. GO & prev_reward==1 & choice>8.5 & ep_trial>=85 has precision 0.125 on 8373 steps, and ep_trial 90-99 has 39 activations in total. The explanation mentions this but leaves it out of the predicate, even though it is the largest structured FP class.
The choice>8 threshold is loose. GO & choice in (8, 9) has precision 0.20 and holds only 3% of mass. Moving the threshold to about 8.8 raises precision from 0.68 to 0.87 and costs only 1.5% of mass.

The second FP class is long rewarded a1 streaks in which the activation decays to 0 (test misses show runs of r1 a1 S1c windows with no activation). The explanation describes this decay, but nothing in the predicate captures it.

The magnitude claim 'strongest on the first rewarded trials after an unrewarded or rare one' is not supported. Among GO & prev_reward==1 & choice>8.5, a first reward after an unrewarded trial (tv('prev_reward',-1)==0) has firing precision 0.67, against 0.78 after two consecutive rewards. Several test windows show the unit silent on the first rewarded trial after an r0 and only rising on the following trials.

Reported test scores reproduce: precision 0.679, recall 1.0, F1 0.809. The observed-only alternative quoted, with the upcoming action, scores precision 0.555 / F1 0.714 on dev. Using choice is not a future variable.
